To kill a Python process on Linux from the command line, you can use the `kill` command. First, identify the process ID (PID) of the Python process using the `ps` command:

```
ps aux | grep python
```

This will list all running Python processes along with their PIDs. Once you have the PID, you can kill the process using:

```
kill -9 <PID>
```

The `-9` flag forcefully terminates the process. Be cautious when using this command as it can cause data loss or corruption if the process is writing to files.
